match_note: The arXiv v1 is a late or final revised version, not the manuscript first reviewed. It lists Kaifa Luo as a coauthor, whom the rebuttal says was added in revision 1, and Zhongxu Wei and Tian Qian, added in revision 2. It also contains material the rebuttals say was added later: 4 K dI/dV maps and anti-phase discussion (round 2); 'extraordinarily high' replacing 'record-high'; a 14 meV gap instead of 13.89 meV; 'Role of electron-phonon-coupling' replacing 'origin of t-CDW'; Fig. 1 bulk/exfoliated labels; Fig. 3e error bars and the AHD definition; DECP phase analysis (round 3); and the 'transverse Peierls transition induced CDW' terminology with red-marked Fig. 2g–i (round 4). Rule used for in_v1: true if the criticized claim, data or figure still exists in v1, even if revised; false if the specific criticized text or element has been removed or corrected in v1.

concerns.quote: I am not sure that we learn anything profound about the so-called t-CDW. In fact, the discussion parts of the paper are rather limited and there is no theoretical support to explain this phenomenon.
concerns.summary: The interpretation and discussion of the claimed transverse CDW are thin and lack theoretical support; R3 likewise found the interpretation weak.

concerns.quote: some explicit labels on the panels could help with clearer identification and more obvious message.
concerns.summary: Fig. 1 panels should be explicitly labelled as exfoliated or bulk samples.

concerns.quote: I am not sure we learn anything more about the origin of the t-CDW from the pump-probe measurements, therefore the figure title and section title “origin of t-CDW” may be inappropriate.
concerns.summary: The pump-probe data only confirm generic CDW signatures, so the 'origin of t-CDW' framing overclaims.

concerns.quote: we are shown data up to only 40 ps, yet the authors report results of the fitting for the slow component decay (tau_s) in the range 10-40 ps. Are the authors reliably able to obtain the slow component
concerns.summary: It is questionable whether a 10–40 ps slow decay constant can be reliably extracted from data shown only to 40 ps.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the dramatic divergence in A_s and tau_s reported in panels b and c, does not seem to be obvious at all by looking at the data curves in panel a.
concerns.summary: The claimed divergence of the slow-component amplitude and lifetime is not visible in the raw ΔR/R curves.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The fit is not clearly visible (dashed line). The language is perhaps inappropriate since both “data” and “fit” show coherent phonons and oscillations
concerns.summary: In Fig. 3d the fit line is not visible and the legend labels are misleading.

concerns.quote: I suggest the authors include error bars similar to other panels, so that we can assess the significance of the mode softening. The inset has no axis ticks. “AHD” should be defined
concerns.summary: Fig. 3e needs error bars to judge the significance of the softening, axis ticks on the inset, and a definition of AHD.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The current discussion is extremely limited and does not offer any real insight. A comparison should be made with other superconducting materials with competing CDW order.
concerns.summary: The thickness dependence of superconductivity and its competition with the CDW are barely discussed and should be compared with other CDW superconductors.

concerns.quote: The figure captions of Fig. 4 are wrong. They seem to be copy-and-pasted from Fig. 3.
concerns.summary: The Fig. 4 captions were copied from Fig. 3 and are incorrect.

concerns.quote: In Fig. 4d, what is “S-metal” and what is “S-CDW”? – it should be written explicitly, and ideally discussed in the main text. In general, the phase diagram is not discussed at all.
concerns.summary: The phase-diagram labels are undefined and the phase diagram is not discussed.

concerns.quote: In Fig. 4 panel c, I suggest to add the 22 nm thickness label as well.
concerns.summary: Fig. 4c is missing a 22 nm thickness label.

concerns.quote: In the abstract, the authors write “ record-high real-space displacement”, but this seems inappropriate.
concerns.summary: 'Record-high' in the abstract is an inappropriate claim.

concerns.quote: they obtain a gap value of “13.89 meV” but I highly doubt the precision of two decimal places.
concerns.summary: The gap value is quoted with unjustified precision.

concerns.quote: the clarity of the following sentence should be improved: “The vanish of CDW transition in bulk strongly indicates the observed occasionally occurrence of the CDW is significantly tuned by the thickness
concerns.summary: A sentence on the bulk absence of the CDW is unclear.

concerns.quote: the STM measurements exhibiting the putative t-CDW at 80 K were performed on cleaved bulk crystals. Figure 4 indicates that the t-CDW does not appear at 80 K (or at any temperature) for the bulk.
concerns.summary: STM sees the modulation on cleaved bulk crystals, while transport and diffraction say bulk samples have no CDW; this is inconsistent.

concerns.quote: A transverse phonon does not cause a modulation of the ionic (or 'superionic') charge density... Why shouldn't the present phenomenon be called a "periodic lattice distortion"
concerns.summary: A transverse distortion need not modulate charge density, so the phenomenon may be a periodic lattice distortion or structural transition rather than a CDW.

concerns.quote: the modulations of occupied and unoccupied states have an anti-phase relationship. Do the Authors have data, or can they perform a measurement, that would display the presence or absence of this behavior?
concerns.summary: Tunneling spectroscopy is needed to show a gap, spatially modulated LDOS and anti-phase contrast between occupied and unoccupied states.

concerns.quote: If the interesting behavior imaged here is characterized as a transverse phonon, i.e. purely a modulation of the phase, why do additional peaks (additional intensity modulations) appear in the FFT?
concerns.summary: A purely transverse (phase) modulation should not produce the extra intensity peaks seen in the FFT, so the interpretation is inconsistent.

concerns.quote: The key information about a transverse displacement should be encoded in phase information in the same result. Can the Authors show that? If possible, the Authors can also try a heterodyne phase detection algorithm
concerns.summary: The authors should show FFT phase information or use Lawler-type heterodyne phase detection to visualize the transverse displacement directly.

concerns.quote: The amplitude of the transverse phonon mode is argued to be about 4 Angstroms even between nearest neighbors, but that is actually larger than the reported a and b lattice constants
concerns.summary: The claimed ~4 Å displacement exceeds the quoted in-plane spacings, raising calibration doubts; R3 asked for STM scale bars to support this bold claim.

concerns.quote: The Authors should include the current set-point used in STM measurements.
concerns.summary: The STM current set-points are not reported.

concerns.quote: The statement in the introduction that CDW "remains absent in superatomic materials" is misleading, especially since the authors later acknowledge prior observations.
concerns.summary: The introduction misstates prior work by claiming no CDW has been reported in superatomic materials.

concerns.quote: The paper would probably benefit from more structural details on the internal dimension of the superatomic cluster in the text
concerns.summary: More detail is needed on the internal structure and dimensions of the superatomic cluster.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It is unclear what is driving such a large CDW displacement. Can the authors at least provide a tentative explanation?
concerns.summary: No mechanism (strong EPC, nesting, transverse nature, or other) is offered for the very large displacement.

concerns.quote: provide some insights about the two-dimensional nature of the CDW observed and address why the CDW appears to be suppressed in bulk samples.
concerns.summary: The authors should explain why the CDW is absent in bulk and appears only in thin samples.

concerns.quote: I think that the current title is too generic, something more specific that gives insight into what kind of anomalies are discussed would be better.
concerns.summary: The title is too generic.

concerns.quote: the caption "Statistics of the distance of between chains along a-axis." is unclear. Also the same figure panel a would benefit from axis inclusion
concerns.summary: The Supplementary Fig. 1 caption is unclear and panel a needs reference axes.

later_concerns.quote: the pump-probe measurements are sensitive only to optical modes at q = 0. So I am not sure that the argument of strong EPC over a broad range of q is valid
later_concerns.summary: Softening of q=0 optical modes cannot support broad-q softening or a strong-EPC mechanism.

later_concerns.quote: the frequency softens from ~0.712 to 0.708 THz across TCDW, or a change of <=0.5%. This seems at odds with the supposed strong EPC
later_concerns.summary: The tiny softening and a 14 meV BCS-like gap point to weak coupling, contradicting the strong-EPC claim.

later_concerns.quote: the origin of the two frequencies should be established, i.e. are they phonons? Or amplitude modes of the CDW? The authors should make it explicit which specific mode is plotted in Fig .3e
later_concerns.summary: The two oscillation modes need clearer presentation, identification of their origin, and a statement of which mode is plotted.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the figure captions for Supplementary Fig. 8 and Fig. 9 are wrong
later_concerns.summary: Supplementary captions are wrong or incomplete, and supplementary figures need bulk/flake labels.

later_concerns.quote: I think there is too large a possibility that the modulations seen in STM and those seen using SAED are not actually exactly the same phenomenon.
later_concerns.summary: The surface-effect explanation is speculative; the STM and SAED modulations may be different phenomena, and LEED or similar is suggested.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the meaningful density should really be the 'column density', integrated over the vertical axis... according to this there would be no CDW in Fig. R7b
later_concerns.summary: The toy model is a periodic lattice distortion; the charge modulation depends on an arbitrary sampling path, and a 'vectorial density' is not a density.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: another possible explanation for the appearance of the STM images is a periodic rotation of the cubes, without any displacement, or some combination of rotation and displacement.
later_concerns.summary: Periodic rotation of the superatom cubes could explain the STM images instead of displacement.

later_concerns.quote: This is only the topography, and not a conductance map... I don't think this shows that there is a charge density modulation, i.e. a modulation of the total 'brightness' of different cubes.
later_concerns.summary: Bias-dependent topography is not a conductance map and shows only intra-cube redistribution, not a modulation of total charge per cube.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: pay attention to wording and grammar (usage of "understanded" comes to mind) and to especially re-check the added parts in the discussion, which sounds a bit clumsy
later_concerns.summary: Grammar and wording need fixing; the title should be reconsidered.

later_concerns.quote: What evidence do they have to support stimulated Raman?... Have the authors checked the phase of the oscillatory signal from the fitting results?
later_concerns.summary: The coherent-phonon mechanism (ISRS vs DECP) should be established from the oscillation phase with a careful time-zero determination.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: if we integrate the total charge density over the vertical axis in Fig. 2(h), we would find that this integrated charge simply has a periodicity of a
later_concerns.summary: The Fig. 2(h) model describes no CDW; a 'transverse CDW' may be impossible, and a longitudinal Peierls-like trimer hopping model is proposed instead.

later_concerns.quote: it is best to calculate images of [dI/dV(V)]/[I(V)/V].
later_concerns.summary: The dI/dV maps should be normalized to avoid the setpoint effect.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: By definition, transverse waves, or shear waves, do not perturb the density. All density waves are longitudinal waves.
later_concerns.summary: A 'transverse CDW' cannot exist, so calling the CDW 'anomalous' in the title is unjustified.

later_concerns.quote: there are a few grammatical errors in the newly added text that should be corrected.
later_concerns.summary: There are grammatical errors in the newly added text.

first_round.quote: In my opinion, the work seems suitable for publication in Nature Communications. In the following, I give some specific comments.
I have a few queries, especially about the STM measurements (which I am well-equipped to evaluate), before I can make a decision about whether the paper should be accepted
I find that the manuscript is a bit weak in the interpretation part. Overall, I believe this work will be worth considering for publication in Nat. Comm. only after appropriate revisions.

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0; the file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. R1 judges the work suitable and asks for mostly presentational fixes plus more discussion, so minor revision. R2 withholds a decision and asks for new STM spectroscopy and phase analysis, and questions whether the effect is a CDW at all, so major revision. R3's level is a judgment call between minor and major. R3 asks for substantial new interpretation (the mechanism of the large displacement, why the CDW is absent in bulk) and a new title, so major revision. R3's comments are misnumbered in the original, with no item 2 and two items numbered 4.
recommendations.label: contested
